title: Wage and role compression arrive before visible organizational restructuring or GDP shifts
text: Under minimal AGI—where reproducible models match average human capabilities at the cost of compute—balanced teams of complementary human specialists still outcompete AI-only firms, leaving firm boundaries and aggregate headcounts largely intact. Yet wages shift immediately: pay for AI-matched generalist tasks compresses toward compute cost while scarce specialists and human coordinators command higher returns. Macro employment stability therefore provides weak evidence that AI is having little economic impact.
qualification: Theoretical equilibrium result from Organizing Intelligence (arXiv:2611.05417) illustrating comparative statics across capability regimes; actual wage pass-through depends on labor-market frictions, institutional contracts, and deployment speed.

public_locator.value: because wage effects arrive before organizational restructuring, macro statistics of employment rates provide poor evidence that AI is not having an effect on the economy.
